chapter: Philadelphia and the McRae Brothers Band, 1908-1929
title: High school band, buying a tenor saxophone
summary: McRae joins the high school band, works in Dr. Miller's drugstore, buys a saxophone from a pawnshop after hearing a tenor solo with Paul Whiteman.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: I couldn't remember. That used to bug me a lot. I always wanted to know who some of those people were, but I didn't bother about it because eventually when I got into high school, I got into the band -- played in the high school band.
I bought my own saxophone. See, I used to work after school in the drug store with Dr. Miller at North Philadelphia (inaudible) 22nd and Susquehanna (inaudible) Avenue, something like that.
And coming home from school one day, I passed the pawn shop. And I saw this beautiful horn in the window. I said, 'Oh, that's for me. I like that.'

Why I got interested in tenor, Paul Whiteman came to Philadelphia one year. My brother took me to see Paul Whiteman and his big band. this boy came down to the mike and And (inaudible) played this beautiful

tenor -- beautiful solo. That's the instrument I wanted to play from then on. I said I wanted to buy me a tenor sax. And I worked and bought my own saxophone.
You hadn't fooled around with a saxophone before?
